body.p: I. Status
Claims 1-20 are pending, of which claims 1, 14, and 18 are independent. In this Office Action:
" Claims 1, 2, 6, 7, 14, 15, 17, and 18 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being
unpatentable over Shimokawa et al. (US 2004/0063501 Al) in view of Hardisty et al.
" Claims 3-5, 8-13, 16, 19, and 20 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected
base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of
the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.

Claims 1, 3-12, 14, and 16-20 have been amended. Claims 2 and 15 have been cancelled. No new matter has been introduced. The claim amendments are supported by at least the original claims and specification as filed. After entry of the claim amendments above, claims 1, 3-14, and 16-20 are pending.
II. Allowable Subject Matter

The Office Action objects to claims 3-5, 8-13, 16, 19, and 20 as being dependent on a rejected base claim, but indicates claims 3-5, 8-13, 16, 19, and 20 would be allowable if rewritten in independent form to include all of the elements of the base claim and any intervening claims. Applicants thank Examiner for the careful review of claims 3-5, 8-13, 16, 19, and 20, but decline to present those claims in independent form at this time. Rather, Applicants present remarks and/or amendments herein directed at refining and placing the entire claim sets in condition for allowance. Applicant submits that these claims are allowable in their current dependent form and respectfully requests that the claim objections be withdrawn.
III. Amendments Not Related to Patentability

Amendments to claims 3-12 and 19-20 have been made not in response to any rejection or objection posed by Examiner, but rather simply to refine the language of those claims. Applicants have broad discretion to choose and modify the language of a claim. It should be noted that, because these amendments to claims 3-12 and 19-20 fall within the bounds of that discretion, such amendments are not related to the patentability of those claims.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the Section 103 rejections. Solely for purposes of advancing the prosecution, Applicant has amended claims 1, 14, and 16-18, and submits that the pending claims are patentable over the cited prior art references under Section 103.
Claim 1 as amended recites a method comprising, inter alia:

p.u: uiring operation attribute information of the tri
er operation in response to the tri
an aim point of the target shooting prop in an aiming direction to a target size that matches the operation attribute information

body.p: determining an object targeted by the aim point as a target object: and

performing, in response to the trigger operation and in a target time period by using the target shooting prop, a plurality of continuous shooting actions on a target area in which the target object is located, wherein the target object is targeted by the target shooting prop.
(emphasis added)
Support for the amendment on claim 1 can be found in at least the original claims 1-2 of the instant application as filed.

As acknowledged by the Office Action, the cited prior art reference of Shimokawa does not explicitly disclose "performing, in response to the trigger operation and in a target time period by using the target shooting prop, a plurality of continuous shooting actions on a target area in which the target object is located, wherein the target object is targeted by the target shooting prop"

as claimed in independent claim 1. Additionally, the cited prior art reference of Hardisty does not disclose the above emphasized features of the amended claim 1 and fails to cure deficiencies of Shimokawa, either. The cited Table 4 of Hardisty discloses that "holding down the Right Trigger 115 will initiate a full auto fire mode" (emphasis added). However, Hardisty fails to teach "performing, ... in a target time period ..., a plurality of continuous shooting actions on a target area" as recited from the amended claim 1. (emphasis added)

In addition, none of the references, alone or in combination, discloses "acquiring operation attribute information of the trigger operation ...; adjusting an aim point ... to a target size that matches the operation attribute information: determining an object targeted by the aim point as a target object" recited in the amended claim 1. For example, as cited by the Office Action, paragraph [0064] of Hardisty at most discloses a manual aiming system that is designed to facilitate the selection of the enemy that the Enslaver attacks, wherein the "manual aiming system will "snap" the Enslaver's manually aimed attacks to the enemy considered closest to the player's intended aim (with closer targets also having priority over more distant ones))". However, neither the cited paragraphs of Hardisty nor Hardisty as a whole teaches "acquiring operation attribute information of the trigger operation ...; adjusting an aim point ... to a target size that matches the operation attribute information: determining an object targeted by the aim point as a target object". Other references fail to cure the above deficiency of Hardisty.

Applicant thus respectfully submits that claim 1, as amended, is patentable over the cited prior art reference. Independent claims 14 and 18 as amended are patentable for at least the same reasons. Other dependent claims being rejected under Section 103 are patentable over the cited prior art references due to at least their dependencies on claim 1, 14, or 18. Applicant respectfully requests that the Section 103 rejections be withdrawn.
VI. Conclusion

Applicant respectfully submits that the patent application is in condition for allowance. If, in the opinion of the Examiner, a telephone conference would expedite the prosecution of the subject application, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned representative.
Respectfully submitted,
